{"design":"Ordering: how meshIRCd's mesh and MIMI's hub disagree, and what the bridge does about it. Written 2026-11-22 after reading meshIRCd's s2s.go and mimid's marmot-bridge.md.

BOTH DECISIONS ARE FIXED AND NEITHER IS OURS.
- MIMI: one hub per room assigns a total order. AGENTS.md: MLS validity alone picks the winning Commit, and the first valid Commit per epoch in hub order wins. MLS requires this — an epoch has exactly one Commit, and divergent commits are divergent groups, which cannot be merged. mimid orders history by (accepted_at, seq), the hub's acceptance time.
- meshIRCd: a mesh with no spanning tree. s2s.go keeps a scalar Lamport counter for ordering (Merge: seq = max(seq, event.seq) + 1) and a per-origin vector map[string]int64 for reconciliation, which SyncRequest carries so a peer can send what is missing. RFC 2813 never needed this because its S2S assumes a cycle-free spanning tree: order is implicit in the topology and a netsplit is repaired by replaying state, not by merging divergence. Once the topology is a mesh, two servers can learn one event by different paths, and the vector clock is the right answer.

So the bridge cannot reconcile the two models. It must pick a reduction and say which.

MOST OF THIS IS ALREADY SOLVED, by marmot-bridge.md, and should be reused rather than redesigned:
- Who the speaker is (§3.2): the real author goes in the content as a prefix for every client, and in a mimiExtensions entry mimid-on-behalf-of for mimid's own front ends and for loop prevention. The MLS sender stays the bridge, which is what AGENTS.md's invariant requires; a front end may show 'Bob (via bridge)' but never as a sender in its own right. This works unchanged for IRC: the label is the IRC nick and network.
- Loops and idempotency (§6.1): an id map keyed by link and direction, with the other side's event id unique per link and direction, plus an idem_key. For Marmot the other-side id is an event id; for meshIRCd it is (origin URN, seq) from the vector clock, which is just as unique. Same table, different column type.
- Late and reorderable arrivals (§6.3): the hold queue with hold_until, built so a copy is not committed to MIMI until it is unlikely to be withdrawn. A mesh's partition-heal replay is the same shape of problem.

WHAT IS GENUINELY NEW, mesh-shaped, and not covered by the Marmot work:

1. Partition replay arrives as new. When a mesh partition heals, SyncResponse delivers a burst of old events. Those the bridge already relayed are dropped by the id map, but ones it never saw are new to it and enter the MIMI room with the hub's current acceptance time. There is no field a hub honours that says 'this happened earlier', so the mesh's order cannot be preserved through the hub. The hold queue reduces how often it happens; it cannot remove it. The bridge must say so rather than imply the transcript is the mesh's history.

2. Concurrent events have no total order, so the transcript order is the BRIDGE's. Two bridges on one link would produce two different MIMI transcripts from the same mesh events. Therefore: exactly one bridge per (MIMI room, IRC channel) link, enforced, failing closed when a second appears. mimid already has the pattern — the state lock and takeover handshake of purple-mimi.md §6 — and it should be reused rather than invented.

3. Convergent membership against Commits a hub may refuse. This is the one with no existing answer. IRC channel membership in a mesh converges by TS rules; MIMI membership is a sequence of MLS Commits the hub checks against room policy and MAY refuse. So the mesh can converge on 'alice is in the channel' while the MIMI room's policy refuses her, and the bridge's only way to push back is to kick her in IRC — which is a new mesh event, which converges, which a concurrent join elsewhere may undo. That is a feedback loop, and a mesh is where loops oscillate. Marmot has no equivalent because Marmot groups are not a mesh with convergent membership.

THE REDUCTION TO PROPOSE, for Mark:
- Messages both ways, with §3.2's speaker labelling and §6.1's id map keyed by (origin, seq).
- Membership one way only, MIMI to IRC. The bridge never turns an IRC join into a MIMI Commit; an IRC user who is not a MIMI participant speaks through the bridge's own leaf, as a Marmot user does.
- One bridge per link, enforced by a lock, failing closed.
- Documented plainly: the MIMI transcript's order is the bridge's linearisation, not the mesh's causal order, and a partition heal can place old IRC lines after newer ones.

That keeps both fixed decisions intact and puts the loss where it can be described, rather than pretending the two orders can be merged. Item 3 is the part worth Mark's eye before any code."}

new_value: {"notes":"Decision mimid-1wgh.96 (Mark, 2026-11-22) settles item 3 of the design field: the channel is a WINDOW onto the room, not a mirror. The bridge announces membership changes and never kicks or invites a real IRC user, so it creates no mesh events and needs no channel operator privileges. IRC-to-MIMI membership was never available: MLS needs a KeyPackage and a plain IRC user has none.\n\nItems 1 and 2 of the design field stand as written: partition replay can place old IRC lines after newer ones and that must be documented rather than hidden, and there is exactly one bridge per link, enforced by a lock on the purple-mimi.md §6 pattern, failing closed."}

{"notes":"Mark's realisation, 2026-11-22: a MIMI-to-IRC gateway is not one gateway, it is one gateway PER IRC S2S PROTOCOL. Confirmed, and it is worse than one codec each.

IRC STANDARDISED ITS CLIENT PROTOCOL AND NEVER ITS SERVER PROTOCOL. The client side is RFC 1459/2812 plus IRCv3 capability negotiation, which is why ONE client-mode bridge reaches every network — and why this bead already specifies client mode ('connects OUT to an IRC network as an IRC client'). The server side fragmented:

- TS6: ircd-ratbox -> charybdis -> solanum, and ircd-hybrid. Widest reach; Libera runs solanum. Spanning tree, SID/UID, SJOIN, TS conflict rules.
- P10: Undernet's ircu and Nefarious. Numeric tokens, quite different.
- InspIRCd's spanning tree: its own, versioned (1205 and so on), shifts across major releases.
- UnrealIRCd: its own, changed substantially across 4, 5 and 6.
- IRCnet: a separate lineage again.
- Ergo: NO S2S AT ALL, single-server by design, so a whole modern ircd is unreachable by this route.
- meshIRCd (Mark's): signed JSON-LD envelopes (@context, @type, @id, sig, sigAlg) with seq and origin for the vector clock, over TLS. Shares no lineage with any of the above.

THE COST IS NOT N PARSERS, IT IS N CONSISTENCY MODELS. Each S2S protocol carries its own, and mapping it onto MIMI's hub order is the expensive part, as the ordering analysis in this bead's design field shows: TS6 and its relatives assume a spanning tree with TS-based conflict resolution, meshIRCd is a mesh reconciled by vector clocks, MIMI is hub-authoritative with exactly one Commit per epoch. Every gateway is a different reconciliation, not a different codec.

CONSEQUENCES.
- Client mode stays the design: one implementation, every network, no trust relationship, no operator vetting.
- Any S2S gateway is a separate project per ircd family. By the reference-not-only rule it is probably not mimid's work at all: a second MIMI implementation is worth more than mimid speaking TS6. If one is ever wanted, TS6 buys the most reach.
- S2S makes sense only where Mark owns both ends, which today means meshIRCd and tailircd.

ON WHICH NETWORKS TO ASK (Mark asked the same day): order is Mark's own networks first, where S2S is fine and the did:webvh and did:key work of mimid-1wgh.97 is already exercised beside mimid on dokr; then ONE small experiment-friendly network in client mode; then large networks in client mode only, later, expecting conditions rather than a yes. docs/design/client-survey.md:242 already records that Libera's Matrix bridge was shut down, which is the base rate for asking a large network to carry a protocol bridge. Any network will require that bridged users are visibly marked, that an operator can ban one individually (helped by decision mimid-1wgh.96: the bridge holds no channel op and never enforces membership), and that channel content does not leave without participants knowing — which is the real obstacle, and symmetric, since E2EE ends at the bridge in both directions.

Strategic weighting: a bridge to a large IRC network buys reach, not MIMI interop evidence, so it should not consume the January interop runway."}
